<style>
.status-circle {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  width: 22px;
  height: 22px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  font-size: 11px;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: white;
  margin-right: 6px;
}

.status-circle.CR { background:#d73027; }
.status-circle.EN { background:#fc8d59; }
.status-circle.VU { background:#fee08b; color:black; }
.status-circle.NT { background:#91bfdb; }
.status-circle.LC { background:#1a9850; }
.status-circle.NE { background:#999999; }
</style>

```{r setup3, include=FALSE}
status_circle <- function(x) {
  code <- if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0 || is.na(x[1]) ||
              !nzchar(as.character(x[1]))) "NE" else as.character(x[1])
  if (isTRUE(knitr::is_html_output())) {
    sprintf('<span class="status-circle %s">%s</span>', code, code)
  } else {
    # Word / PDF: HTML spans don't render, so use a plain bracketed code.
    sprintf("[%s]", code)
  }
}
```

```{r setup, include=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: apply consistent styling to every Word/PDF flextable.
#   ft            — a flextable object
#   caption_text  — string used as the table caption (bolded, full table width)
#   header_labels — optional named list to relabel headers; use "\n" to force a
#                   line break, e.g.  list(`Long Column Name` = "Long Column\nName")
# Centred columns, autofit to 100% page width, booktabs theme with bold header,
# compact font/padding so headers don't push the table off the page.
style_pdf_table <- function(ft,
                            caption_text  = NULL,
                            header_labels = NULL) {
  ft <- flextable::set_table_properties(ft, layout = "autofit", width = 1)
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, align = "center", part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::theme_booktabs(ft, bold_header = TRUE)
  ft <- flextable::fontsize(ft, size = 9, part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::padding(ft, padding = 4, part = "all")
  if (!is.null(header_labels)) {
    ft <- do.call(flextable::set_header_labels,
                  c(list(x = ft), header_labels))
  }
  if (!is.null(caption_text)) {
    ft <- flextable::set_caption(
      ft,
      caption = flextable::as_paragraph(flextable::as_b(caption_text)),
      align_with_table = FALSE)   # let caption span page width, not just table
  }
  ft
}
# evaluate some parameters

# Defensive loader: returns NULL when the param is NULL, NA (the YAML default),
# an empty vector, or a vector containing only NAs.  Without this, terra::rast()
# would be called on NA and the report would crash before any chunks rendered.
.load_rasters <- function(files) {
  if (is.null(files)) return(NULL)
  files <- files[!is.na(files)]
  if (length(files) == 0) return(NULL)
  lapply(files, terra::rast)
}

rasters        <- .load_rasters(params$raster_files)
rasters_change <- .load_rasters(params$rasters_change_files)
years <- params$years %||% numeric(0)
n <- length(rasters)

terraOptions(progress = 0)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Which descriptive variables were requested?  Used to (a) build a single
# consolidated "X, Y and Z were not requested" sentence at the top of the
# Ecosystem description section, and (b) conditionally show / hide section
# and tab headers so empty sections don't appear in the report at all.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
descriptive_flags <- list(
  typology    = !is.null(params$typology),
  countries   = !is.null(params$countries),
  rainfall    = !is.null(params$rainfall),
  temperature = !is.null(params$temperature),
  elevation   = !is.null(params$elevation)
)

# Human-friendly labels (display order matches report layout)
descriptive_labels <- c(
  typology    = "Global Ecosystem Typology",
  countries   = "Geographic distribution by country",
  rainfall    = "Rainfall",
  temperature = "Temperature",
  elevation   = "Elevation"
)

missing_labels <- unname(descriptive_labels[
  names(descriptive_flags)[!unlist(descriptive_flags)]
])

# Build a single sentence listing missing variables.  Returns "" if none missing.
not_requested_sentence <- (function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0) return("")
  if (length(x) == 1) {
    paste0("*", x, " was not requested for this ecosystem.*")
  } else if (length(x) == 2) {
    paste0("*", x[1], " and ", x[2], " were not requested for this ecosystem.*")
  } else {
    paste0("*The following descriptive variables were not requested for this ",
           "ecosystem: ", paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "),
           ", and ", x[length(x)], ".*")
  }
})(missing_labels)

# Abiotic tabset helpers --------------------------------------------------
any_abiotic   <- any(unlist(descriptive_flags[c("rainfall", "temperature", "elevation")]))
first_abiotic <- if (any_abiotic) {
  names(which(unlist(descriptive_flags[c("rainfall", "temperature", "elevation")])))[1]
} else NA_character_

tab_header <- function(name, label) {
  if (!isTRUE(descriptive_flags[[name]])) return("")
  if (!is.na(first_abiotic) && first_abiotic == name) {
    paste0("#### ", label, " {.active}")
  } else {
    paste0("#### ", label)
  }
}
```

# **Report summary**

This report documents an ecosystem assessment following the IUCN Red List of Ecosystems (RLE) Guidelines, for the `r ecosystem_label` `r if(length(params$years) == 0) {        "with no raster years uploaded"      } else if(length(params$years) == 1) {        paste("using data from", params$years)      } else {        paste("using data between", min(params$years), "and", max(params$years))      }`. This report has been created from the Ecosystem Classification Assessment Tool (EcoCAT) developed as part of the EcoCAT project from RBG Kew. 

 - This tool and report currently covers **Criterion A** and **Criterion B** of the RLE assessment. 
 - The graphs in this report can be downloaded by selecting the 'download as png' icon at the top of each graph.
 - To download the data and mapping files as part of this assessment, please revisit the 'Report/Data download' tab in the tool, select the required data files for download and select the 'Download data' button.

```{r mapped_distribution, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.align="center", out.width="100%", eval = !is.null(rasters) && length(rasters) > 0}
# Always-shown recent + loss map.  Uses the same figure helpers as the app tab
# (figures.R sourced by the Shiny app at startup, in scope at render time).
#
# r_loss is taken from `rasters_change` if available; otherwise NULL, in which
# case make_fig_loss / make_fig_distribution_leaflet falls back to showing just
# the most recent raster.
r_recent <- rasters[[length(rasters)]]
r_loss   <- if (is.null(rasters_change)) {
  NULL
} else if (inherits(rasters_change, "SpatRaster")) {
  rasters_change
} else if (is.list(rasters_change) && length(rasters_change) > 0) {
  rasters_change[[length(rasters_change)]]
} else {
  NULL
}

if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  make_fig_distribution_leaflet(r_recent, r_loss, years)
} else {
  make_fig_loss(r_recent, r_loss, years)
}
```
